run.researchNotes: Company run on Punjab National Bank: 27 web searches plus page fetches (Screener, Indian Kanoon and some broker pages were refused by the fetch allowlist). BASIS: STANDALONE throughout; three full standalone statements reconcile (assets = liabilities: FY26 Rs 19,87,327.25 cr, FY25 Rs 18,19,806.84 cr, FY24 Rs 15,62,887.77 cr; CFO+CFI+CFF = change in cash; closing cash = cash with RBI + balances with banks). Lender layout: revenue = interest earned; employeeCost + otherExpenses + depreciation = reported operating expenses; operating profit minus PBT gives provisions (FY26 Rs 2,539.93 cr, FY25 Rs 1,674.60 cr, FY24 Rs 11,736.60 cr). Depreciation is the consolidated figure (standalone not separately published in sources read); see conflicts. dividendsPaid = prior-year DPS x prior-year shares. FY25 equityRaised is the announced Rs 5,000 cr QIP. FY26 tax rate of 36.8% reflects the switch to the new tax regime (Q1 FY26 tax Rs 5,083 cr). Quarterly: Q2 FY27 interest expense, other income, PBT and tax derived from rounded press-release totals; employee/other opex split not found for any quarter (totals reconcile: Q1 FY27 Rs 7,612.63 cr, Q4 FY26 Rs 7,041.93 cr, Q3 FY26 Rs 8,073.79 cr); quarterly EPS only for Q2 FY27. Model: the interest split by asset is the standalone FY26 schedule (advances, investments, RBI/inter-bank, others), which sums exactly to interest earned; volumes are FY25-FY26 average balances. Model tax rate is the 25.17% statutory rate, not FY26's DTA-inflated 36.8%. Capex 1.2% of revenue is an ASSUMPTION; ESOP set to 0 because no outstanding scheme was found (verify). Valuation: FY27 PAT of Rs 21,000 cr, ABV roll-forward, ECL deduction, ROE inputs, beta and ERP are assumptions. Price is the 12 Nov 2026 close (13 Nov close not found). Performance: m1 and m3 are to 29 Oct 2026 (Oquilia); m6 and m12 are to 6 Nov 2026 (Upstox); relative returns not established. Forensic decade: profits for FY17-FY26 found; operating cash flow found only for FY22-FY26; FY16 loss (Rs 3,974.39 cr) recorded in timeline. capitalAllocation FY23 return is the directors'-report ROE. Not established: weekly price series, current 200-DMA, 52-week low date, impact cost, ten-year P/B median, Sustainalytics numeric score, Sep-2026 CET1 (Sep-2025 consolidated 12.78% used), current PNB Housing stake, top-20 borrower concentration, emphasis-of-matter and auditor-tenure flags, full names of current Executive Directors. Sector backdrop (macro, industry, regulation, competition, sector valuation, TAM/SAM/SOM) is carried from the PSU-bank sector run in this session.

industry.structure: India has 12 public sector banks, led by SBI with about a fifth of system advances, followed by a mid-tier of Bank of Baroda, PNB, Canara and Union, a second tier of Indian Bank and Bank of India, and four small banks (Central, IOB, UCO, PSB) plus Bank of Maharashtra. PSBs held 54.4% of bank loans at Dec 2025, up from 53.11% a year earlier, as their loan growth of 18-28% outran private banks' low-to-mid teens. The government owns a majority of every PSB, from just over half at SBI to about 93% at Punjab & Sind Bank, which shapes capital raising, pay, merger decisions and float. PSBs earned a record Rs 1.98 lakh cr in FY26, up 11%.
industry.cyclePosition: Late expansion. Non-food credit is growing 19.1%, GNPA is at multi-decadal lows and credit costs are near cycle troughs (SBI 0.22% in Q2 FY27), which is where earnings peak. The rate cycle turned with the 7 Oct 2026 hike and CPI above 6%, and ECL lands on 1 Apr 2027, so provisions are more likely to rise than fall from here. Loan growth running well ahead of deposit growth across PSBs is the classic late-cycle signal.
industry.profitPool: SCB profit after tax rose to Rs 4,05,268 cr in FY26 (RBI FSR, Jun 2026), of which PSBs earned about Rs 1.98 lakh cr, roughly 49%. The pool is moving toward PSBs: Q2 FY27 PSB PAT grew ~27% YoY vs ~24% for private banks (MOFSL), and PSB NIMs held while private-bank NIMs fell 8-20bp. Within PSBs, SBI earned about 40% of group profit in Q3 FY26. Part of the Q2 FY27 gain was treasury and one-off income (BoB treasury Rs 4,093 cr; SBI stake-sale gain), which will not recur at this level.
industry.technologyShift: Distribution is now almost entirely digital: 98.8% of SBI transactions ran through alternate channels in Q1 FY27. PSBs are moving MSME underwriting to digital-footprint models (Rs 41,500 cr sanctioned in eight months of 2025). Globally, agentic AI, fintechs and stablecoins (>$300bn) are eroding customer stickiness, and ECL demands PD/LGD/EAD models with forward-looking macro inputs that most PSBs are still building.

regulation.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (prudential and monetary), with the Ministry of Finance - DFS as owner of PSBs and SEBI for listing and public-shareholding rules
regulation.rules: Banking Regulation Act 1949 and the Bank Nationalisation Acts of 1970/1980; Basel III capital (system CRAR 17.2% at Sep 2025); priority-sector lending targets; the new Commercial Banks - Asset Classification, Provisioning and Income Recognition Directions 2026 introducing three-stage ECL from 1 Apr 2027 while retaining NPA classification; FDI in PSBs capped at 20%.
regulation.underReview: ECL transition (loans fair-valued on 1 Apr 2027, transition period to 31 Mar 2031); PSB consolidation; MPS compliance for four PSBs; policy stance moved to calibrated tightening on 7 Oct 2026 with the next MPC on 2-4 Dec 2026.
regulation.costOfChange: ICRA expects the ECL impact on capitalisation to be moderate, but Vinod Kothari expects it to hurt bank profits and retained earnings in FY28; RBI rejected requests for more time and PSB stocks fell up to 2.5% on 28 Apr 2026. Bank-level day-one ECL estimates were not found.

companies.name: Punjab National Bank
companies.business: India's second-largest public sector bank, 70.08% owned by the Government of India, which absorbed Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India on 1 April 2020. At 30 Sep 2026 its global business was Rs 31.18 lakh cr: deposits Rs 17.77 lakh cr (CASA 36.6%) and advances Rs 13.41 lakh cr, through 10,481 branches. It earns mainly net interest income (Rs 41,960 cr in FY26 standalone) plus fees, treasury and write-off recoveries (other income Rs 18,794 cr). It owns PNB Gilts, PNB Investment Services and PNB Cards, holds 30% of PNB MetLife and 13% of Canara HSBC Life, and remains a promoter of PNB Housing Finance.
thesis: FY27 standalone profit reaches about Rs 21,000 cr (H1 Rs 10,785 cr) with ROA above 1%, as core operating profit grows 25-30% and credit cost stays near 0.25%.
Global NIM recovers from 2.50% (Q1 FY27) toward the 2.60-2.70% guide as MCLR rises and the RAM and gold book reprices.
The Rs 9,000-10,000 cr ECL transition is absorbed from profit without equity, leaving CRAR above 16.5% and adjusted book compounding at 12%+.

theses.claim: FY27 standalone profit reaches about Rs 21,000 cr with ROA above 1%.
theses.mechanism: Core operating profit (excluding treasury and write-off recoveries) rose 29.4% to Rs 5,971 cr in Q2 FY27 and is now 79% of operating profit, against 64% a year earlier. Credit cost is 0.25% and slippage 0.77%, inside the 0.9% guide, so pre-provision profit converts almost fully to profit. The tax rate has normalised after the FY26 switch to the new regime cost Rs 5,083 cr of tax in Q1 FY26. It fails if ECL front-loading or a slippage spike hits H2.
theses.evidence: Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 5,253.29 cr and Q2 Rs 5,532 cr (H1 Rs 10,785 cr); Q2 ROA 1.05%, ROE 17.32%, cost-to-income 45%; FY26 PAT Rs 16,903.99 cr after a 36.8% tax rate.
theses.size: About Rs 21,000 cr PAT, EPS about Rs 18.3 (+24% on FY26's Rs 14.71).

theses.claim: Global NIM moves back toward the 2.60-2.70% FY27 guide.
theses.mechanism: NIM fell from 3.09% (FY24) to 2.57% (FY26) as repo cuts repriced loans before deposits. Deposit costs are now falling (domestic cost of deposits 4.97% in Q2 FY27 vs 5.16% in FY26), the bank raised MCLR by 10bp from 1 Nov 2026, and the fastest-growing books (gold +97%, retail +16.3%) carry higher yields. Q2 already recovered 8bp QoQ to 2.58%. It breaks if term deposits reprice up faster than loans as the CD ratio climbs past 75%.
theses.evidence: Global NIM 2.50% (Q1 FY27) to 2.58% (Q2 FY27); domestic NIM 2.74%; FY27 guide 2.60-2.70%; MCLR +10bp effective 1 Nov 2026.
theses.size: Each 5bp of NIM on about Rs 18 lakh cr of average earning assets is roughly Rs 900 cr of annual NII.

theses.claim: ECL is absorbed without an equity raise and adjusted book keeps compounding.
theses.mechanism: MD Ashok Chandra sized the ECL impact at about Rs 9,000-10,000 cr and 75-85bp of CRAR in Oct 2025. By Q2 FY27 the bank had built an additional Rs 1,150 cr standard provision, put the remaining loan-book requirement near Rs 5,000 cr, and noted Rs 4,000 cr of IFR reserves that may be usable. Against CRAR of 17.95% and annual profit near Rs 21,000 cr, the hit is about half a year's earnings.
theses.evidence: Reuters interview (Oct 2025): about Rs 9,000 cr, CRAR -0.85pp; Q2 FY27 call (16 Oct 2026): Rs 1,150 cr ECL standard provision, about Rs 5,000 cr remaining; CRAR 17.95% (Sep 2026).
theses.size: Post-ECL Mar-27E ABV of about Rs 129; at 1.0x that is Rs 129, about 9% below the Rs 141.79 price.

moat.barrier: A 130-year-old deposit franchise with 10,481 branches, strongest in north India and enlarged by the 2020 OBC and United Bank merger, plus 70.08% sovereign ownership that underpins AAA ratings on its Tier II bonds.
moat.evidence: Global deposits grew 9.9% to Rs 17.77 lakh cr (Sep 2026) and CASA is 36.6%, well above most PSU peers; Ind-Ra, Crisil and CareEdge rate its Tier II AAA mainly on government support. But CASA fell from 38% (Q1 FY26) toward 36-37% and growth relies on term deposits.
moat.testSurvived: Survived the FY16-FY19 cycle only with government capital: net losses of Rs 3,974 cr (FY16), Rs 12,283 cr (FY18, including the Rs 14,357 cr Nirav Modi-Mehul Choksi LoU fraud) and Rs 9,975 cr (FY19). The deposit base held; shareholder returns did not.
moat.durability: Moderate. Sovereign backing and the CASA base are durable; the cost advantage depends on holding CASA above 36%.

capitalAllocation.summary: The decade splits at FY21. FY16-FY19 brought losses totalling about Rs 26,000 cr (FY16 -Rs 3,974 cr, FY18 -Rs 12,283 cr, FY19 -Rs 9,975 cr), repeated GoI recapitalisation and the April 2020 merger with OBC and United Bank. Since FY23 profit has compounded (Rs 2,507 cr to Rs 16,904 cr), the dividend rose from Rs 0.65 (FY23) to Rs 3.00 (FY26, about 20% payout), the bank raised about Rs 5,000 cr by QIP in FY25 above book, and sold 10% of Canara HSBC Life for Rs 912 cr. ROE averaged below the cost of equity until FY25.

mispricing.concern: "FY26 profit grew only 1.6% - PNB has stopped growing."
mispricing.answer: FY26 PAT was held back by a 36.8% tax rate after the switch to the new tax regime (Q1 FY26 tax Rs 5,083 cr); operating profit grew 9.2% and PBT 6.3%. With tax normalised, H1 FY27 PAT of Rs 10,785 cr is already 64% of FY26's full year.

mispricing.concern: "NIM has fallen from 3.09% to 2.5% - margins are structurally broken."
mispricing.answer: The fall is real and pricing power is scored Weak. But Q2 FY27 NIM rose 8bp QoQ, deposit costs are falling and MCLR was raised from 1 Nov 2026; core operating profit grew 29% in Q2 because opex fell, not because of margin.

mispricing.concern: "PNB is the Nirav Modi bank - governance will bite again."
mispricing.answer: The Rs 14,357 cr fraud (2018) and the Rs 2,434 cr SREI-linked fraud (Dec 2025) are fully provided, and RBI penalties in 2026 are small currency-chest lapses (about Rs 1.8 cr in total). Governance is scored Weak, not Poor; the risk is operational control across 10,481 branches, of which unaudited branches carry 25% of advances.

mispricing.concern: "At 1.1x book after a 45% run from its low, the re-rating is done."
mispricing.answer: This is the strongest objection and the valuation accepts it: the base case of Rs 129 at 1.0x post-ECL book is below the price, and brokers' Rs 140 targets are roughly the current price. The stock needs ROE near 16% to justify 141.79.

exports.evidence: Overseas presence is small (a Dubai branch, GIFT City, representative offices); Moody's, Fitch, CareEdge rated a USD 1.5 bn MTN in Sep 2026; overseas share not disclosed.

capacity.evidence: CRAR 17.95% (Sep 2026) funds 13-14% loan growth; ECL takes about 75-85bp of CRAR; no capital raised in FY26 despite approval for Rs 8,000 cr.

execution.evidence: Met FY26 asset-quality guidance (PCR 97.14%) and H1 FY27 credit and cost goals, but NIM has missed the guide in two straight quarters.

longevity.evidence: Deposit-taking and lending will be needed in fifteen years; 70.08% GoI-owned, issuer rated IND AAA/Stable (affirmed Dec 2025).

dcf.evidence: Base value Rs 129 (1.0x post-ECL Mar-27E ABV of about Rs 129) is about 9% below the Rs 141.79 close of 12 Nov 2026.

growthAdjustedValuation.evidence: P/E of 7.72x on FY27E EPS growth of about 24% (Rs 21,000 cr vs Rs 16,904 cr) gives a PEG near 0.3, flattered by FY26's tax-hit base.

fcfYield.evidence: Free cash flow is not meaningful for a bank; the earnings yield is 13.0% (TTM EPS Rs 18.37 / Rs 141.79) against a 7.15% 10-year G-sec (10 Nov 2026).

marginOfSafety.evidence: Price of Rs 141.79 is about 10% above the Rs 129 base case; the bear case of Rs 95 implies a 33% loss.

impliedExpectations.evidence: At about 1.10x post-ECL ABV, 15% COE and 6% growth, the price implies a sustained ROE of about 15.9%, vs 12.5% in FY26 and 17.3% in Q2 FY27.

scenarioAsymmetry.evidence: Bull upside of Rs 16 (to Rs 158) is less than bear downside of Rs 47 (to Rs 95), at probabilities 25/50/25.

catalystAdjusted.evidence: Dated catalysts: MPC 2-4 Dec 2026, Q3 FY27 results in late Jan 2027 with the ECL path, and ECL go-live on 1 Apr 2027.

balanceSheet.evidence: Leverage ratios do not apply to a bank; CRAR 17.95% (Sep 2026) against an 11.5% minimum and PCR 97.32%; CET1 12.78% at Sep 2025 (consolidated).

accounting.evidence: Unmodified FY26 joint audit, but unaudited branches carried 25.01% of advances; CFO swung from -Rs 27,895 cr (FY24) to +Rs 26,302 cr (FY26); FY26 PAT hit by DTA.

governance.evidence: Material frauds recur: Rs 14,357 cr LoU fraud (2018), Rs 2,434 cr SREI-linked fraud (Dec 2025); RBI currency-chest fines of about Rs 1.8 cr across 2026.

promoter.evidence: Government of India holds 70.08%, unchanged for four quarters to Sep 2026, with no pledge.

customerConcentration.evidence: Granular book: retail ex-IBPC +16.3%, MSME about Rs 2.03 lakh cr (Q4 FY26) of Rs 13.41 lakh cr; top-borrower concentration not disclosed in sources read.

regulatory.evidence: ECL from 1 Apr 2027 with a one-time impact of about Rs 9,000-10,000 cr (Oct 2025 estimate), about 6-7% of FY26 net worth and 75-85bp of CRAR.

cyclicality.evidence: Losses at the last trough: FY18 net loss Rs 12,283 cr and FY19 Rs 9,975 cr, with GNPA at 18.38% in Mar 2018.

competition.evidence: Deposits +9.9% vs advances +14.7% (Sep 2026), CD ratio up to 75.5% from 72.3%, CASA slipping from 38% to 36.6%, so funding cost pressure rises.

technology.evidence: Digital transactions +31% YoY (Q2 FY27); no capability gap named by management or regulators in sources read.

execution.evidence: Mostly delivers on credit, asset quality and cost, but missed NIM guidance in Q1 and Q2 FY27 and did not use its FY26 fund-raising approval.

liquidity.evidence: Average NSE turnover of Rs 238.76 cr a session over 20 sessions to 28 Oct 2026 (20.2 mn shares); F&O stock; a large position exits in days.

geopolitics.evidence: Limited overseas book (Dubai branch, GIFT City); USD 1.5 bn MTN programme and FCNR(B) raising tie a small part of funding to the rupee.

valuationRisk.evidence: P/B of about 1.14x is above the 0.85-0.98x of Sep 2026 and near a multi-year high; a return to 0.9x would cost about 20%.

dilution.evidence: Rs 5,000 cr QIP in FY25 lifted shares 4.4% to 1,149.29 cr; Rs 8,000 cr raise was approved for FY26 but not used; no ESOPs or convertibles found.

financialQuality.evidence: Ten years include losses in FY16, FY18 and FY19 (Rs 26,232 cr in total); ROE reached 14% only in FY25 and fell to 12.5% in FY26.

managementGovernance.evidence: Guidance met on credit and cost, missed on NIM; a Rs 2,434 cr fraud reported Dec 2025 and seven RBI penalties in 2026 show control gaps.

technicalEntry.evidence: Close of Rs 141.79 on 12 Nov 2026 followed a Rs 143.80 intraday 52-week high on 62.1 mn shares, 3.1x the 20-session average; extended after +7% in three sessions.

catalysts.evidence: Three dated catalysts with mechanisms: MPC 2-4 Dec 2026, Q3 FY27 results in late Jan 2027, ECL go-live 1 Apr 2027.

sectors.name: Advances (loan book)
sectors.evidence: Interest and discount on advances was Rs 88,761.59 cr in FY26. On average net advances of Rs 1,151,383 cr (mean of Rs 10,77,475 cr at Mar-25 and Rs 12,25,292 cr at Mar-26) that is a yield of 7.709%, and 1,151,383 x 0.077091 = 88,761. Volume grows 13%, inside the raised FY27 credit-growth guide of 13-14% and below the 14.7% delivered to Sep-26. Yield drifts up 0.3% a year because MCLR was raised 10bp from 1 Nov 2026 and RAM/gold loans (gold book +97% to about Rs 36,000 cr) are growing fastest. The margin is the spread over a 5.01% FY26 cost of funds; global NIM recovered from 2.50% (Q1 FY27) to 2.58% (Q2). The four sectors sum to Rs 128,223 cr against FY26 standalone interest earned of Rs 1,28,223.19 cr (gap 0.0001%, rounding of yields only; the split is the bank's own standalone interest schedule).

sectors.name: Investments
sectors.evidence: Income on investments was Rs 33,125.77 cr in FY26 on average investments of Rs 495,712 cr (Rs 4,97,311 cr and Rs 4,94,112 cr), a yield of 6.682%; 495,712 x 0.066825 = 33,126. The book shrank 0.6% in FY26 as funds moved to loans and the CD ratio rose to 75.5%, so volume is held at 6% (SLR needs grow with deposits of 9-10%). Yield is held flat: AFS reserves turned negative (-Rs 128 cr at Sep-26) as G-sec yields hardened. The four sectors sum to Rs 128,223 cr against FY26 standalone interest earned of Rs 1,28,223.19 cr (gap 0.0001%, rounding of yields only; the split is the bank's own standalone interest schedule).

sectors.name: Balances with RBI and banks, money at call
sectors.evidence: Interest on balances with RBI and other inter-bank funds was Rs 4,257.77 cr in FY26 on average cash and bank balances of Rs 155,333 cr (Rs 1,48,720 cr and Rs 1,61,947 cr), a yield of 2.741%; 155,333 x 0.027411 = 4,258. CRR balances earn nothing, so this line yields far less than the 5.01% cost of funds and its gross margin is negative; it is liquidity, not a profit centre. Volume grows 3%. The four sectors sum to Rs 128,223 cr against FY26 standalone interest earned of Rs 1,28,223.19 cr (gap 0.0001%, rounding of yields only; the split is the bank's own standalone interest schedule).

sectors.name: Other interest
sectors.evidence: Other interest of Rs 2,078.06 cr in FY26 (Rs 1,493 cr FY25, Rs 539 cr FY24; largely interest on income-tax refunds) has no economic volume driver. It is scaled against average other assets of Rs 86,824 cr only so the base year ties: 86,824 x 0.023934 = 2,078. Held flat, with margin set at the bank-wide FY26 NII to interest-earned ratio of 32.72%. The four sectors sum to Rs 128,223 cr against FY26 standalone interest earned of Rs 1,28,223.19 cr (gap 0.0001%, rounding of yields only; the split is the bank's own standalone interest schedule).

valuation.method: Price to adjusted book using the justified multiple (ROE - g)/(COE - g) on Mar-2027E ABV after deducting NNPA and the one-time ECL impact. Stakes in PNB MetLife (30%), Canara HSBC Life (13%), PNB Housing Finance and the listed PNB Gilts are noted but not added. Banks are not valued on FCF DCF, EV or ROCE.

base.assumptions: 1.0x post-ECL Mar-2027E ABV of about Rs 129: FY26 book Rs 124.12 plus about Rs 21,000 cr FY27 profit less the Rs 3.00 dividend gives Rs 139.39 BV, less Rs 2.99 NNPA (Rs 3,433 cr, Jun 2026) and Rs 7.83 of ECL (Rs 9,000 cr). Justified P/B (15-6)/(15-6) = 1.0x.

plausibility.3x@3-5: Implausible on base drivers: book grows about 12-13% a year after ECL (about 1.8x in five years) and a re-rating from 1.1x to 1.5x would give only about 2.4x.

multibagger.chain: System credit of about Rs 213.6 lakh cr grows 12-14% and PNB holds about 5.9% share. Interest income grows 11-13%, NIM of 2.6% and ROA of about 1% give PAT of about Rs 21,000 cr in FY27, about 80% is retained, and book grows 12-13% after ECL. A multiple of 0.9-1.2x book gives 8-15% annual returns plus a 2% yield, not a multibagger.

variantPerception.marketBelieves: PNB's earnings have turned: tax has normalised, cost-to-income fell to 45% and asset quality is the best in a decade, so the stock broke out to a new 52-week high at about 1.1x book.
variantPerception.researchIndicates: The earnings recovery is real (core operating profit +29%), but NIM is still below guide, ECL will take about Rs 9,000 cr, and ROE on average book was 12.5% in FY26, so 1.1x post-ECL book already prices ROE near 16%.
variantPerception.difference: The market and brokers (Rs 140 targets) value PNB at or above book before deducting ECL; the research view deducts ECL and NNPA and finds the base case about 9% below the price.
variantPerception.evidence: Q2 FY27: PAT Rs 5,532 cr (+12.8%), NIM 2.58% vs 2.60-2.70% guide, cost-to-income 45%; ECL about Rs 9,000-10,000 cr; price Rs 141.79 (12 Nov 2026) vs base Rs 129.
variantPerception.consequence: The stock is fully valued after the breakout; better entry lies nearer 1.0x post-ECL book (about Rs 125-130) unless NIM reaches 2.65% and ROE holds above 16%.

bearCase.argument: PNB has the worst history among large PSBs: losses of Rs 26,000 cr in FY16-FY19, India's largest bank fraud, and another Rs 2,434 cr fraud reported in Dec 2025. Its NIM has fallen 50bp in two years and keeps missing guidance, deposits grow 5 points slower than loans, ECL will take Rs 9,000-10,000 cr and the stock has re-rated 45% from its low to 1.1x book. A normal credit cycle would wipe out two years of profit.
bearCase.answer: Most of this is fair and is scored (resilience and cyclicality Poor, governance Weak, margin of safety Poor). The answer is that the balance sheet entering ECL is the cleanest in a decade (NNPA 0.25%, PCR 97%), core profit is accelerating, and CRAR is 17.95%. The bear value is plausible, which is why the reward-to-risk at Rs 141.79 is unfavourable.
